speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start by locating the pain: can you point to exactly where on your neck and arm the pain and weakness are most severe? Additionally, do you notice any specific movements that make your symptoms worse?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful; can you describe whether the weakness or numbness follows a specific pattern, such as affecting only your thumb and index finger, or if it spreads to your whole arm? Also, have you noticed any muscle wasting or twitching in your hands recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS).

I am requesting a detailed neurological exam focusing on upper and lower motor neuron signs, and I request the MRI of your brain and cervical spine to rule out compressive myelopathy. Additionally, please submit results for Nerve Conduction Studies/EMG and Serum Creatine Kinase.
